program_name: Aerospace Engineering — the official ENGLISH title used on the University's orientation portal. This is a STANDALONE degree, not an English curriculum inside an Italian degree, which confirms the research brief's "type: standalone". BUT IT IS NOT AN ENGLISH-TAUGHT DEGREE: the official Italian title is "Ingegneria Aerospaziale" and the diploma reads "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Aerospaziale". The binding Didactic Regulations state it plainly in Art. 1: "Il presente Regolamento disciplina gli aspetti organizzativi del Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Aerospaziale (classe LM-20, IdSua: 1573407). Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Aerospaziale (Aerospace Engineering, in inglese) afferisce al Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale. Il corso e bilingue (italiana, inglese). Il corso e erogato in modalita convenzionale." So "Aerospace Engineering" is the English rendering of an Italian-titled, officially BILINGUAL degree. MINISTERIAL COURSE ID: IdSua 1573407. ADMINISTERING DEPARTMENT: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale (DII, Department of Industrial Engineering, http://www.dii.unina.it). SCHOOL/FACULTY: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School, SPSB). Teaching area recorded centrally: "Ingegneria". Duration 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS. THREE INTERNAL SPECIALISATIONS ("indirizzi", chosen at enrolment): (1) Aeronautics / Aeronautica, (2) Fluid Dynamics and Propulsion / Fluidodinamica-Propulsione, (3) Space / Spazio. These are tracks inside the SAME degree; they do not change the diploma title and they are declared to the Student Office rather than requiring an individual study plan. Which track you pick is nevertheless the single most important decision for a non-Italian-speaking applicant, because the amount of English-taught teaching differs enormously between them (see teaching_language). level: master (Italian "Laurea Magistrale", second-cycle degree, 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS), confirming the research brief. The central unina.it course record states "Tipo di corso: Magistrale | Durata: 2 anni | Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1 livello"; the orientation portal fact-sheet header reads "Master's Degree — Aerospace Engineering (LM) | Degree required: Laurea I Livello". The Student Guide cover reads "CORSO DI LAUREA MAGISTRALE IN INGEGNERIA AEROSPAZIALE — Classe delle Lauree Magistrali in Ingegneria Aerospaziale e Astronautica, Classe LM-20". CREDIT STRUCTURE (a.y. 2026/2027 study plan, orientation portal): Related or Supplementary Modules (TAF C) up to 15 ECTS; Characterising Modules (TAF B) up to 66 ECTS; Elective Modules at the student's free choice (TAF D) up to 15 ECTS; Further Training Activities (TAF F) up to 12 ECTS; Final examination (TAF E) 12 ECTS. Total 120. One CFU = 25 hours of total student workload; contact teaching is 8 hours per CFU for lectures, tutorials, seminars and laboratory work (Art. 6 of the Didactic Regulations). YEAR 1: two "related/supplementary" modules chosen from Table A (one 9-ECTS module in semester 1, one 6-ECTS module in semester 2); four compulsory 9-ECTS characterising modules that DIFFER BY SPECIALISATION (36 ECTS); optionally the annual 9-ECTS "Aerospace Design Project" (three 3-ECTS modules: Structures, Systems, Fluid dynamics) common to all three tracks. YEAR 2: characterising modules chosen from the track's own table (B1 Aeronautics / B2 Fluid Dynamics and Propulsion / B3 Space) up to the 66-ECTS total — normally two 9-ECTS plus two 6-ECTS exams, or one 9-ECTS plus two 6-ECTS if the Aerospace Design Project was taken in year 1; plus 15 ECTS of free-choice modules, 12 ECTS of Further Training Activities and the 12-ECTS final examination. FURTHER TRAINING ACTIVITIES (12 ECTS, TAF F) — normally 3 ECTS of "further language knowledge" plus 9 ECTS of internship. The ordinamento caps the components at max 6 CFU language, max 3 CFU IT skills, max 12 CFU internships, max 3 CFU other employability knowledge; the study-plan note fixes the standard split at 3 + 9. INTERNSHIPS ARE COMPULSORY (Art. 17: "Le attivita di tirocinio e stage sono obbligatorie") and may be intramoenia (in University laboratories) or extramoenia (in companies or bodies with a University agreement); either may feed directly into the thesis, certified on the "AC form" countersigned by the internship supervisor or thesis supervisor. FINAL EXAM (12 ECTS): assessment by an academic committee of a master's thesis prepared under a university supervisor, covering theoretical, numerical and/or experimental work carried out in a University laboratory, an external research laboratory, or an Italian or foreign company. External tutors may attend as co-supervisors but do not sit on the examining board. The committee is chaired by the Programme Coordinator (or the most senior member present). PRESENTATION LENGTH — the two official sources disagree: the Didactic Regulations say "La presentazione ha una durata compresa di norma in 15 minuti", the orientation portal says "The presentation usually lasts 12 minutes". STUDY PLAN DEADLINE: a new or amended individual study plan must be submitted by 31 OCTOBER each year (extended automatically if the enrolment deadline is extended); non-submission simply keeps the previously approved plan with no possibility of variation. The Didactic Coordination Commission (CCD) must rule on a submitted plan within four weeks. Students who pick one of the three published tracks and follow notes (a)-(d) get an AUTOMATICALLY APPROVED plan and need only notify the Student Office of the chosen track.
teaching_language: [uncertain] BILINGUAL ITALIAN/ENGLISH — AND THIS IS THE DECISIVE FIELD FOR THIS PROGRAMME. The orientation portal fact-sheet header records "Language ENG/ITA" (the Italian-language version of the same page records "Lingua ITA/ENG"); the Didactic Regulations state "Il corso e bilingue (italiana, inglese)". The programme is NOT an English-taught degree and is NOT listed among the English-taught Master's degrees in the University's International Course Catalogue — it appears there only under "Double degrees", tagged "ITA/FRA" (ISAE-ENSMA Poitiers) and "ITA/SPA" (Universidad de Sevilla). This VERIFIES the research brief's note that the programme is not in the official international course catalogue. THE GOVERNING RULE, printed under every study-plan table in the Didactic Regulations: "Tutti gli insegnamenti sono offerti in italiano, tranne quelli contrassegnati da *, che sono offerti esclusivamente in lingua inglese" (all modules are offered in Italian, except those marked with *, which are offered EXCLUSIVELY in English). The orientation portal repeats it in English: "All courses marked with an asterisk are taught in English and the corresponding examinations must be taken in English." So an asterisked module is English-only — lectures AND examination — and a non-asterisked module is Italian-only. There is no dual delivery of the same module. HOW MUCH ENGLISH YOU ACTUALLY GET DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH OF THE THREE TRACKS YOU CHOOSE — this is the single most important practical finding of this record: (1) SPACE TRACK (Indirizzo Spazio) — EFFECTIVELY 100% ENGLISH-DELIVERABLE. All four compulsory first-year modules are asterisked: Space Structures (9*), Space Systems (9*), Space Flight Dynamics (9*), Space Propulsion (9*). Table A offers an English option in BOTH slots (Mathematical Methods for Engineering 9* in semester 1; Reliability and Risk in Aerospace Engineering 6* in semester 2). The optional annual Aerospace Design Project (9*) is English. EVERY module in Table B3 is asterisked: Hypersonic Aerodynamics (9*), Aerospace Remote Sensing Systems (9*), Space Mission Design (9*), Spacecraft Dynamics and Control (6*), Space Experiments (6*), Launch and Re-entry Vehicle Design and Dynamics (6*). Table C also contains English options. A Space-track student who deliberately selects the asterisked options can therefore complete all 120 ECTS in English and write and defend the thesis in English. (2) FLUID DYNAMICS AND PROPULSION TRACK — PARTLY ENGLISH. Of the four compulsory first-year modules only Space Propulsion (9*) is English; Numerical Fluid Dynamics (Fluidodinamica Numerica, 9), Dynamics and Flight Simulation (Dinamica e simulazione di volo, 9) and Aircraft Aerodynamics (Aerodinamica dei velivoli, 9) are ITALIAN-ONLY — 27 of the 36 compulsory ECTS are in Italian. Table B2 is mostly English (Hypersonic Aerodynamics 9*, Experimental Fluid Dynamics 9*, Aeroelasticity 6*, Fluid-Structure Interaction 6*, Space Experiments 6*, Fluid Dynamic Stability 6*) but Rotating Wing Aerodynamics (6) and Turbulence (6) are Italian. (3) AERONAUTICS TRACK — THE MOST ITALIAN. NONE of the four compulsory first-year modules is asterisked: Advanced Aerospace Structures (Strutture Aerospaziali Avanzate, 9), Dynamics and Flight Simulation (9), Aircraft Aerodynamics (9) and Avionics (Avionica, 9) are ALL ITALIAN-ONLY — the full 36 compulsory ECTS in Italian. Only the Table A options and much of Table B1 (Numerical and Experimental Methods for Aircraft Design 9*, Unmanned Aircraft Systems 9*, Aeroelasticity*, Air Traffic Management and Control 9*, Aircraft Operations 6*, Aircraft Design 9*, Fluid-Structure Interaction 6*, Aircraft On-Board Systems 6*, Flight Testing 6*) are English, while Aerospace Structures II (9), Structural Dynamics (9) and Rotating Wing Aerodynamics (6) are Italian. A NON-ITALIAN SPEAKER CANNOT COMPLETE THE AERONAUTICS TRACK. OTHER LANGUAGE-RELEVANT FACTS: delivery is fully conventional and in person ("modalita convenzionale", "In presenza" for every module) — there is no blended/MOOC component as in some other Federico II degrees. The thesis and its defence MAY be in English: "La relazione scritta e la discussione potranno essere sviluppate in inglese" (Art. 16). Free-choice modules (15 ECTS, TAF D) may be taken from the other tracks' tables or Table C without an individual study plan, or from anywhere in the Polytechnic School / Erasmus with an approved individual plan — most of the wider School catalogue is Italian-taught, so a non-Italian speaker must pick the asterisked options deliberately. MARKED [uncertain] BECAUSE: the asterisk list is published per academic year and can change year to year (the 2026/2027 orientation-portal tables and the 2025/2026 Didactic Regulations annex already differ on the credit value of Aeroelasticity — 9 vs 6 ECTS); the department's own Manifesto pages were still showing A.A. 2025/2026 at the time of research; and no unina.it page states in so many words that any track is fully deliverable in English — that conclusion is derived by summing the asterisked modules. Confirm the current asterisk list with michele.grassi@unina.it or alfredo.renga@unina.it before committing.

admission_type: OPEN ACCESS WITH A COMPULSORY ADMISSION CHECK — the orientation portal labels it "Admission: Verifica di preparazione" (verification of preparation), NOT "Libero". Note this label carefully: it is not the same wording Federico II uses for its plainly free-access master's degrees, and it signals that admission is conditional even though there is no competition for places. There is NO numerus clausus, NO seat cap, NO ranked selection, NO bando and NO TOLC. The programme does not appear anywhere in the University's index of "Corsi a numero programmato" for a.y. 2026/2027 (the only two-year master's degrees listed there are Precision Livestock Farming, Professioni sanitarie, Psicologia Clinica e degli interventi, Scienze Enologiche and Scienze della Nutrizione Umana). ADMISSION IS A TWO-PART GATE, both parts compulsory (Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations, echoed at School level by the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base): (1) POSSESSION OF THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS — an L-9 Industrial Engineering degree or equivalent, or at least 84 CFU in named subject groups (see academic_requirements); and (2) VERIFICATION OF THE ADEQUACY OF THE STUDENT'S PERSONAL PREPARATION. Verbatim: "La verifica della personale preparazione e obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari" (the personal-preparation check is compulsory in every case, and only students who already hold the curricular requirements may take it). If the curricular requirements are missing, enrolment is NOT permitted; the CCD instead determines "integrazioni curriculari" that must be completed BEFORE enrolling, by taking single course units (Corsi Singoli, http://www.unina.it/-/5601348-iscrizione-ai-corsi-singoli) and passing their examinations. THE PERSONAL-PREPARATION CHECK HAS AN AUTOMATIC PASS: "La verifica di adeguatezza della personale preparazione si ritiene automaticamente soddisfatta dagli studenti per i quali la media delle votazioni (in trentesimi) conseguite negli esami di profitto per il conseguimento del titolo di Laurea che da accesso al Corso di Laurea Magistrale — pesate sulla base delle relative consistenze in CFU — sia non inferiore a 24." In plain terms: a CFU-weighted bachelor examination average of at least 24/30 clears this gate automatically. Below 24/30 the case goes to the CCD, which may look at grades in characterising subjects, or set an interview or a written test, or impose curricular integrations (see entry_exam_or_test). AUTOMATIC CURRICULAR ELIGIBILITY: "The curriculum requirements are automatically fulfilled by graduates in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Naples Federico II." THREE PRACTICAL ROUTES. (1) ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION APPLICANTS: apply for admission using the forms on the School's student-forms page, then enrol online at www.segrepass.unina.it. (2) EU CITIZENS, AND ANYONE (including non-EU citizens) LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU, HOLDING A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION: no competitive application and no Universitaly pre-enrolment — per international.unina.it they "have unrestricted access to university courses if you hold a foreign qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification. In this case you have to send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements." For this degree that means Prof. Michele Grassi (michele.grassi@unina.it), with Prof. Alfredo Renga (alfredo.renga@unina.it) as the international-students contact. (3) NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD: compulsory pre-enrolment on the UNIVERSITALY portal, a pre-acceptance letter issued by the Programme Coordinator after document evaluation, then a study visa. Because the course is open access, its non-EU pre-enrolment window closes on 15 June 2026 and does not reopen (see application_deadline_non_eu). [uncertain] NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ADMISSION PAGE FOR INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS EXISTS. Unlike several other Federico II master's degrees, this one publishes no annual one-page "admission rules" sheet in English, no application form for foreign qualifications and no stated evaluation timetable. Everything international is handled through the generic University channels plus direct e-mail to the Coordinator.
academic_requirements: A first-cycle degree (Laurea triennale / Bachelor), plus EITHER an L-9 Industrial Engineering class degree OR at least 84 CFU distributed across named subject groups, plus the personal-preparation check. (A) THE BASE REQUIREMENT (Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations): "L'iscrizione alla Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Aerospaziale richiede il possesso della Laurea, ivi compresa quella conseguita secondo l'ordinamento previgente al D.M. 509/1999, o del diploma universitario di durata triennale o di altro titolo conseguito all'estero riconosciuto equipollente" — a Laurea (including pre-D.M. 509/1999 degrees), a three-year university diploma, or a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent. (B) THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT — TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES. Route 1: hold a degree in the Italian class L-9 "Ingegneria Industriale" (Industrial Engineering) or an equivalent qualification. Route 2: have earned AT LEAST 84 CFU across the two groups below. This is the route a foreign applicant will normally be assessed against, and it is quantified, not discretionary: GROUP 1 — 42 CFU, in the (post-2023) sectors 09/IINF-05 Sistemi di elaborazione delle informazioni; 01/MATH-02 Algebra e Geometria; MATH-03/A Analisi Matematica; 01/MATH-04 Fisica Matematica; 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie; 02/PHYS-01, 02/PHYS-02, 02/PHYS-03, 02/PHYS-04 (experimental and theoretical physics); STAT-01/B Statistica per la ricerca sperimentale e tecnologica; IIND-03/B Disegno e metodi dell'ingegneria industriale. In pre-reform codes (as still published on the central unina.it record) these are ING-INF/05, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/07, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/03, SECS-S/02, ING-IND/15. GROUP 2 — 42 CFU, in 08/CEAR-06 Scienza delle Costruzioni; 09/IIND-06 Macchine e sistemi per l'energia e l'ambiente; 09/IIND-04 Tecnologie e sistemi di lavorazione; 09/IMAT-01 Scienza e tecnologia dei materiali; 09/IIET-01 Elettrotecnica; IIND-07/A Fisica tecnica industriale; IIND-01/C Meccanica del Volo; IIND-01/D Costruzioni e Strutture Aerospaziali; IIND-01/E Impianti e Sistemi Aerospaziali; IIND-01/F Fluidodinamica; IIND-01/G Propulsione Aerospaziale — OF WHICH AT LEAST 18 CFU MUST BE IN THE FIVE CORE AEROSPACE SECTORS: IIND-01/C Flight Mechanics, IIND-01/D Aerospace Structures, IIND-01/E Aerospace Systems and Installations, IIND-01/F Fluid Dynamics, IIND-01/G Aerospace Propulsion. In pre-reform codes: ICAR-08, ING-IND/03, /04, /05, /06, /07, /08, /10, /16, /22, /31, of which at least 18 CFU in ING-IND/03, /04, /05, /06, /07. IN PLAIN TERMS: expect to need roughly 42 CFU of maths, physics, chemistry, statistics, computing and engineering drawing; 42 CFU of mechanics/thermo/materials/electrical engineering and aerospace subjects; and CRITICALLY at least 18 CFU that are specifically AEROSPACE (flight mechanics, aerospace structures, aerospace systems, fluid dynamics, aerospace propulsion). That 18-CFU aerospace core is the requirement most likely to block a general mechanical, civil, physics or mathematics graduate. AUTOMATIC ELIGIBILITY: "The curriculum requirements are automatically fulfilled by graduates in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Naples Federico II." (C) IF YOU FALL SHORT: enrolment is refused, not conditioned. Art. 5: "L'iscrizione al Corso di Laurea Magistrale non e consentita in difetto dei requisiti minimi curriculari." The CCD (possibly through a dedicated investigating commission) then assesses your record, recognises credits in whole or in part, MAY declare equivalences with sectors other than those listed "sulla base dei contenuti di specifici insegnamenti presenti nella carriera pregressa dello studente" (on the basis of the actual content of specific courses you have taken — this is the discretionary escape hatch for foreign transcripts that do not map onto Italian SSD codes), and then sets "integrazioni curriculari" you must complete BEFORE enrolling, via single course units (Corsi Singoli) and their examinations. (D) THE PERSONAL-PREPARATION THRESHOLD: automatically satisfied with a CFU-weighted bachelor examination average of at least 24/30. Below that, the CCD decides — see entry_exam_or_test. (E) THE LANGUAGE COMPONENT OF THE PERSONAL-PREPARATION CHECK (Art. 5, and this is easy to miss): "La verifica di adeguatezza della personale preparazione include anche la verifica del possesso di adeguate competenze linguistiche. Le studentesse e gli studenti non in possesso di un titolo di studio ottenuto a seguito della frequenza di un corso di studio erogato in lingua italiana o inglese, in assenza di certificazioni o idoneita linguistiche relative alla conoscenza della lingua italiana o inglese almeno a livello B1 del QCER, dovranno dimostrare, in un test di idoneita, di possedere adeguate capacita di comprensione e conversazione in italiano o in inglese." So: if your bachelor was taught in Italian or English, or you hold a B1+ certificate in Italian or English, you are through; otherwise you sit an aptitude test. [uncertain] NO MINIMUM DEGREE GRADE is published beyond the 24/30 average threshold, and no unina.it page states how a foreign grading scale is converted into the Italian thirtieths scale for that calculation — a decisive question for any non-Italian applicant. No unina.it page for this programme lists which foreign bachelor titles are considered "equipollenti" to L-9. Confirm both points with michele.grassi@unina.it before applying.
entry_exam_or_test: NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO PORTFOLIO, AND NO ENTRANCE EXAM FOR MOST APPLICANTS — but there IS a conditional written test with a PUBLISHED QUESTION BANK, and it is entirely in Italian. NO TOLC: the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base runs the TOLC only for BACHELOR degrees — "la Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base ... effettua un test di orientamento non selettivo ma obbligatorio per tutti gli immatricolandi ai Corsi di Laurea dei Collegi di Ingegneria e di Scienze" — and applies a different regime to two-year master's degrees: "L'ammissione ai Corsi di Laurea Magistrale non a ciclo unico prevede, ai sensi del DM 270/04, la verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari nonche la verifica della personale preparazione dello studente." No TOLC-I or TOLC-B applies here. THE DEFAULT PATH IS A DOCUMENTARY CHECK: with a CFU-weighted bachelor examination average of at least 24/30 you are automatically exempt from any assessment of personal preparation. Applicants clearing that bar submit the admission-of-graduates form and are assessed on the transcript alone. THE CONDITIONAL PATH — BELOW 24/30. The department's orientation page: "Requests for admission to the Master's course by students who do not meet the criteria for automatic admission must be submitted using the forms available at the following link (pre-evaluation for lower average) and will be examined by the CCD, which will assess the admissibility of the request and determine any requirements that the interested party must fulfil in order to be admitted to the course. The board of examiners may examine the curriculum followed by the candidate, possibly taking into account the marks obtained in characterising subjects or in subjects considered particularly relevant ..., or by establishing assessment methods (interview or test) to verify the adequacy of the student's personal preparation, or by adopting the method foreseen for curricular integration. If the assessment method is a test, the student will be presented with a multiple-choice questionnaire selected from those available at the following link." So the CCD has three tools: transcript analysis, an interview or written test, or compulsory curricular integrations. THE PUBLISHED QUESTION BANK — a genuinely unusual level of transparency, and a warning for non-Italian speakers. The linked PDF, https://aerospaziale.dii.unina.it/images/lm/Test_Ammissione_Media_Insufficiente_LM_Aerospaziale.pdf ("Test Ammissione Media Insufficiente LM Aerospaziale"), contains the full pool of multiple-choice questions (three options each, a/b/c) organised into FIVE subject sections: "Test Meccanica del volo" (Flight Mechanics), "Test Aerodinamica" (Aerodynamics), "Test Propulsione Aerospaziale" (Aerospace Propulsion), "Test Sistemi Aerospaziali" (Aerospace Systems) and "Test Strutture Aerospaziali" (Aerospace Structures). EVERY QUESTION AND ANSWER IS WRITTEN IN ITALIAN — e.g. "L'anemometro di un velivolo misura: a) La velocita vera rispetto all'aria b) La velocita equivalente c) La velocita indicata". No English version is published. The bank has roughly 25-40 questions per section. THE LANGUAGE APTITUDE TEST (a separate, second possible test). Art. 5: students who did NOT obtain their qualification from a course delivered in Italian or English, and who hold no certificate or idoneita at CEFR B1 or above in Italian or English, "dovranno dimostrare, in un test di idoneita, di possedere adeguate capacita di comprensione e conversazione in italiano o in inglese" — an aptitude test of comprehension and conversation in Italian OR English. No format, date, venue or pass mark is published. A THIRD POSSIBLE ASSESSMENT, FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS ONLY: the University's 2026/2027 non-EU booklet states that for programmes taught in Italian, where no recognised Italian certificate is available, "the University will arrange a remote interview. In this case, you will be contacted directly by the examination board." Whether that applies to this bilingual degree is the central open question of this record — see language_requirements and uncertainty_notes. NO INTERVIEW IS ANNOUNCED as a routine step for applicants above the 24/30 threshold, and no unina.it page publishes an academic interview format for this programme. ATTENDANCE ONCE ADMITTED: teaching is delivered conventionally and in person ("modalita convenzionale", every module marked "In presenza"); internships and stages are compulsory as part of the 12-CFU Further Training Activities. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: there is no cut-off score to beat and no ranking list. The real gates are the 84-CFU curricular requirement (including the 18 CFU of core aerospace subjects), the 24/30 average threshold, the language checks, and — for non-EU applicants — the visa pipeline. language_requirements: [uncertain] THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK FIELD IN THIS RECORD, AND THE OFFICIAL SOURCES CONFLICT. There are THREE distinct language rules operating at three different levels, and they do not agree on whether a non-EU applicant needs ITALIAN. RULE 1 — PROGRAMME LEVEL, FOR ADMISSION: B1 in ITALIAN **OR** ENGLISH, and only if you cannot show a prior degree taught in one of those languages. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations: "La verifica di adeguatezza della personale preparazione include anche la verifica del possesso di adeguate competenze linguistiche. Le studentesse e gli studenti non in possesso di un titolo di studio ottenuto a seguito della frequenza di un corso di studio erogato in lingua italiana o inglese, in assenza di certificazioni o idoneita linguistiche relative alla conoscenza della lingua italiana o inglese almeno a livello B1 del Quadro Comune Europeo di Riferimento (QCER), dovranno dimostrare, in un test di idoneita, di possedere adeguate capacita di comprensione e conversazione in italiano o in inglese." Read literally, an English-medium bachelor's degree, or a B1 English certificate, satisfies the programme's own admission language rule, and NO ITALIAN IS REQUIRED. Note also that this is only B1, not B2. RULE 2 — PROGRAMME LEVEL, FOR GRADUATION: B2 in a EU language OTHER THAN ITALIAN, in practice English, satisfied through 3 of the 12 "Further Training Activities" credits. This is NOT an entry requirement and NOT a barrier to enrolment. The programme's own "Operational guidelines for the assessment of English language skills" page states: "since the Master's degree requires students to be fluent in a language of the European Union other than Italian, the regulations stipulate that students who do not have a certificate of knowledge of a language of the European Union at least at B2 level must spend at least 3 of the 12 ECTS provided for training activities in the form of additional language knowledge. The 3 ECTS are not awarded a grade, but only an aptitude." TWO ROUTES: (a) already hold a B2 (CEFR) English certificate from an accredited centre outside the University — send it to the Course Secretariat and request recognition of the 3 ECTS; (b) sit the CLA (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) B2 Placement Test, whose schedule is published at https://www.cla.unina.it/placement_test — the CLA then reports the result to the Coordinator for the 3-CFU recognition. Students who fail the placement test "can follow an online improvement course for level B2 organised by the CLA (https://www.cla.unina.it/bacheca) and then take the test again." No closed list of accepted certificate providers and no recency rule (such as the two-year limit some other Federico II degrees impose) is published for this programme. Separately, a B2 CEFR English certificate IS a hard prerequisite to compete for the Universidad de Sevilla double-degree place. RULE 3 — UNIVERSITY LEVEL, FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT: B2 ITALIAN for programmes taught in Italian. international.unina.it: "If you choose a three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course in ITALIAN, a B2 level Italian language proficiency is required", demonstrated either by uploading a CLIQ-system Italian certificate (Universita per Stranieri di Perugia or Siena, Roma Tre, Societa Dante Alighieri, Universita per Stranieri Dante Alighieri di Reggio Calabria) to Universitaly, or by taking an Italian language proficiency test whose "procedures and timing will be communicated by e-mail by the coordinator of the chosen course", with the result certified in the pre-enrolment application. The 2026/2027 non-EU booklet repeats: "For programmes taught in Italian, students must demonstrate a B2 level (CEFR)" and "If no certificate is available, the University will arrange a remote interview. In this case, you will be contacted directly by the examination board." The exemption clause — "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required" — does not obviously cover a bilingual two-year master's, and Aerospace Engineering is NOT listed among the English-taught degrees in the University's International Course Catalogue. THE CONFLICT, STATED PLAINLY: the programme's own regulations accept B1 English with no Italian; the University's non-EU pre-enrolment rules require B2 ITALIAN for Italian-taught degrees; and this degree is officially "bilingue (italiana, inglese)" and absent from the English-taught catalogue. A NON-EU APPLICANT SHOULD THEREFORE ASSUME B2 ITALIAN MAY BE DEMANDED AT THE UNIVERSITALY STAGE and must resolve this in writing with pre-enrolment@unina.it and michele.grassi@unina.it BEFORE booking a language test. This is not a theoretical risk: the Italian test result has to be certified inside the pre-enrolment application, so discovering the requirement late can cost an entire intake year. THE PRACTICAL LANGUAGE REALITY OF THE DEGREE ITSELF, whatever the paperwork says: only the SPACE track can be completed without Italian. The Aeronautics track's entire 36-CFU compulsory core is Italian-only, and the Fluid Dynamics and Propulsion track's is 27/36 Italian-only. The published admission test question bank is in Italian only. Programme announcements, the Manifesto degli Studi, study-plan forms and much of the department website exist in Italian first. Italian is therefore, in practice, close to essential for the Aeronautics and Fluid Dynamics tracks and merely useful for the Space track. ITALIAN COURSES: the University Language Centre (CLA, https://www.cla.unina.it/) offers international students free self-study online Italian courses through the ICoN Consortium at CEFR A1-C1, and runs B1/B2 English workshops and the Cambridge English, IELTS, TOEFL/TOEIC and PTE Academic examinations. VISA-SIDE NOTE: international.unina.it advises that "an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation", so upload whatever English certificate you hold to Universitaly regardless. OUTPUT LANGUAGE: the thesis and its defence may be written and delivered in English — "La relazione scritta e la discussione potranno essere sviluppate in inglese" (Art. 16) — so the degree can be completed in English at the output end even though much of the input is Italian.
application_deadline_eu: There is NO programme-specific application deadline for EU (and EU-equivalent) candidates, because Aerospace Engineering is open access: EU applicants do not compete for places, they clear the curricular and personal-preparation checks and then enrol within the University's calendar. THREE DATE SETS APPLY. (A) ADMISSION EVALUATION — NO FIXED DATE, DO IT EARLY. Italian-qualification holders submit the admission-of-graduates form (School student-forms page) and are assessed by the CCD; holders of a FOREIGN qualification who are EU citizens, or non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or the EU, must per international.unina.it "send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements" — for this degree, Prof. Michele Grassi (michele.grassi@unina.it), with Prof. Alfredo Renga (alfredo.renga@unina.it) as the international-students contact and uff.didattica.dii@unina.it as the department teaching office. Allow time: if you fall short of the 84 CFU or the 24/30 average, the CCD may impose curricular integrations that must be completed by single course units BEFORE enrolment, which can cost a semester or more. (B) UNIVERSITY ENROLMENT CALENDAR FOR A.Y. 2026/2027, from the binding "Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27", governing Italian and EU students alike: — 2026-07-16: ordinary immatriculation period opens ("16 LUGLIO 2026 - Inizio periodo ordinario immatricolazione"). The first-instalment table specifies "Dal 16 luglio (immatricolazioni L o iscrizioni I anno LM)". — 2026-09-01: ordinary period opens for transfers and course changes. — 2026-11-02: ORDINARY DEADLINE for immatriculation and for re-enrolment in later years ("2 NOVEMBRE 2026 - Scadenza periodo ordinario immatricolazione e iscrizione agli anni successivi"); also the deadline for the ISEEU income data to be retrievable from the INPS database. — 2026-11-03: extraordinary (late) enrolment period opens. — 2027-01-15: last date to enrol late with a EUR 50 surcharge. — 2027-01-16: from this date the late surcharge rises to EUR 110. — 2027-03-31: ABSOLUTE FINAL DEADLINE for first-year enrolment in a two-year master's degree — "Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027", with the condition that a Teaching Coordination Commission may require anyone enrolling after 2026-12-31 to first earn between 6 and 12 CFU via single course units (whose fees are refunded if the master's enrolment is completed by 31 March 2027). Instalments: 1st (60% of the contribution + regional tax + EUR 16 stamp) by 2026-11-02; 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01; 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30. (C) PROGRAMME-LEVEL DEADLINE THAT ACTUALLY BINDS YOU: 31 OCTOBER — the study plan. "E' possibile presentare un nuovo piano di studio, per la prima volta oppure a variazione di quello gia presentato, entro il 31 Ottobre di ogni anno" (extended automatically if the enrolment deadline is extended). Students who pick one of the three published tracks and follow the standard notes only have to NOTIFY the Student Office of the chosen track within the same window; anything else requires an individual study plan submitted through the department's Microsoft Forms procedure with a self-certified bachelor transcript ("autocertificazione storico della carriera triennale" from SegrePass) and "Modulo A" attached, ruled on by the CCD within four weeks. PROCEDURE: Italian students enrol online at www.segrepass.unina.it. BUT ANYONE HOLDING FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP CANNOT USE THE ONLINE ROUTE — the 2026/27 enrolment guide states "Coloro che presentano una cittadinanza straniera dovranno effettuare l'iscrizione presso gli sportelli delle Segreterie Studenti, non potranno usare la procedura on-line." For this degree that means the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80, 80125 Napoli (segreing@unina.it), in person. TEACHING CALENDAR: semesters run roughly September-February and February-July (international.unina.it: "Courses can start as early as September/October and, generally, are held through the end of May/middle of June"). The engineering-specific academic and examination calendar is published at https://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/calendario-delle-attivita-didattiche-del-collegio-di-ingegneria/ and the dynamically updated examination calendar at http://aerospaziale.dii.unina.it/en/info-lm-en ; graduation session dates at https://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/esame-di-laurea-collegio-degli-studi-di-ingegneria/ . application_deadline_non_eu: For NON-EU applicants RESIDING ABROAD there is a hard, ministry-driven three-date pipeline for a.y. 2026/2027, published in the University's official booklet "INFORMATION FOR NON-EU STUDENTS WITH RESIDENCY ABROAD — Admission to Degree Programmes at University of Naples Federico II 2026/2027" and repeated on international.unina.it: — 2026-06-15: PRE-ENROLMENT APPLICATION DEADLINE on the UNIVERSITALY portal, naming the University of Naples Federico II and this programme. Verbatim: "JUNE 15 2026 — Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." THIS IS THE OPERATIVE DEADLINE FOR AEROSPACE ENGINEERING: because the programme is open access (not restricted access), non-EU pre-enrolment closes on 15 June 2026 and does NOT reopen. — 2026-11-30: deadline for lodging the study-visa application at the Italian Embassy/Consulate ("NOV 30 2026 — Deadline for submitting the visa application at Italian Embassies/Consulates"). — 2027-01-31: deadline for completing enrolment (matriculation) in Naples — "JAN 31 2027 — Deadline for completing enrolment at University of Naples Federico II. After this date students who are not officially enrolled according to ministerial regulations will have their visa revoked, and Italian police authorities will be notified." THE PIPELINE IN THREE STAGES, per the booklet: APPLICATION (register on the Universitaly Portal, complete and submit the pre-enrolment application), VALIDATION (the University reviews the application and verifies admission), then the VISA. The pivotal document is the PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER: "A pre-acceptance letter certifies your eligibility for the selected degree programme. It is issued by the Programme Coordinator following an evaluation of the documents you have submitted." For this degree the Programme Coordinator is Prof. Michele Grassi (michele.grassi@unina.it). Sequencing advice from the University: "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme before applying on Universitaly. Otherwise, if you have already submitted your pre-enrolment application on Universitaly, a dedicated team will forward your documents for evaluation. In this case, processing times may be longer." Because this programme publishes NO admission page for international applicants and NO evaluation timetable, contacting the Coordinator early is not optional in practice. Central contact: pre-enrolment@unina.it (put the programme name in the subject line). UNIVERSITY-LEVEL WARNINGS: pre-admission does not guarantee a visa; a visa does not guarantee enrolment; enrolment remains subject to verification of documents and admission requirements even after the student has obtained a visa, travelled to Italy and holds a scholarship. Final enrolment must be completed IN PERSON at the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80, 80125 Napoli (segreing@unina.it) — foreign citizens cannot use the online SegrePass procedure. NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU are treated like EU applicants: "Non-European candidates, wherever they reside and regularly residing in Italy or in a European Union country, have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification", they present documents directly to the course Coordinator and "will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal". They follow the calendar in application_deadline_eu instead. [uncertain] TWO TIMING RISKS SPECIFIC TO THIS PROGRAMME. (1) THE ITALIAN LANGUAGE TEST SITS INSIDE THE DEADLINE. If the University treats this bilingual degree as "taught in Italian" (see language_requirements), the Italian B2 certificate or the University-arranged remote interview must be completed and "certified in the pre-enrolment application" — i.e. BEFORE 15 June — which effectively pulls the real deadline months earlier. Resolve this with pre-enrolment@unina.it as the very first step. (2) NO PUBLISHED EVALUATION LEAD TIME. The programme states no turnaround for the Coordinator's document evaluation and pre-acceptance letter, so build in a generous margin. TIMING NOTE FOR READERS: this record was compiled on 2026-08-30, by which date the 15 June 2026 non-EU pre-enrolment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 HAD ALREADY PASSED. A non-EU applicant reading this must target a.y. 2027/2028 and re-check the dates when the new booklet is published (typically around May).
required_documents: [uncertain] THERE IS NO CONSOLIDATED CHECKLIST ON THE PROGRAMME SITE — this programme publishes no annual admission sheet and no international-applicant document list, so the list below is assembled from the School's admission procedure plus the University-level booklet, admission regulation and enrolment guide. The CCD or the Segreteria could request an additional item. (1) FOR THE PROGRAMME'S OWN ADMISSION ASSESSMENT (all applicants): an application for admission on the School form ("admission of graduates"), plus a transcript detailed enough for the CCD to verify Art. 4 — i.e. showing every examination with its credits AND its subject-sector classification, because the requirement is expressed in CFU per SSD/GSD (42 + 42, of which at least 18 in the five core aerospace sectors). Applicants below the 24/30 weighted average must instead use the "pre-evaluation for lower average" form. Bachelor degree certificate. Evidence of the language condition — a prior degree taught in Italian or English, or a certificate at CEFR B1 or above in Italian or English; failing that, you sit the aptitude test. An existing B2 English certificate should also be sent to the Course Secretariat to claim recognition of the 3 CFU of "further language knowledge". NOTE: the School form links published on the programme's orientation page were unusable at the time of research (one returns HTTP 404) — request the current forms from uff.didattica.dii@unina.it. (2) FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT ON UNIVERSITALY (uploaded as PDF), Master's-degree track, per the University's 2026/2027 booklet: "Transcript of Records (ToR); Final degree certificate; Detailed course descriptions; Additional documents e.g. language certificates, motivation letter, reference letters; Pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator; DoV or CIMEA both Statement of comparability and verification." "Detailed course descriptions" matter more here than for most degrees, because they are what lets the CCD map foreign courses onto the Italian SSD groups and, where necessary, "individuare eventuali equivalenze di crediti di settori scientifico disciplinari differenti ... sulla base dei contenuti di specifici insegnamenti". Also required in the application: personal data exactly as on the passport, and the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested. Where the programme counts as Italian-taught, the Italian B2 certificate or the outcome of the University-arranged remote interview must also be certified in the application. (3) QUALIFICATION-RECOGNITION DOCUMENTS (mandatory at enrolment): a DECLARATION OF VALUE (DoV) issued by an Italian Embassy/Consulate — or, as an alternative, the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND Statement of Verification JOINTLY (https://www.cimea.it/EN/). For qualifications from European Higher Education Area / Bologna Process countries a Diploma Supplement with a CIMEA Statement of Verification is used. "At the enrolment stage, the above-mentioned documents are mandatory and must accompany the submitted/declared academic qualifications." (4) FOR THE ITALIAN EMBASSY / VISA: the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; language certificates; proof of economic means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year; the sum needed for repatriation (a return ticket is acceptable proof); suitable accommodation in Italy; and adequate medical/hospitalisation insurance cover valid in Italy with no limitations or exceptions on emergency hospitalisation rates. (5) FOR ENROLMENT (MATRICULATION) AT THE STUDENT OFFICE, international students: copy of passport (shown, plus one copy left at the office); application form; 1 passport photo; Italian tax code (codice fiscale — you may start without it, but must obtain it to complete enrolment; the Student Office can generate the fee payment notices meanwhile); residence permit or proof of having applied for it; Declaration of Value or ENIC-NARIC/CIMEA certificate; proof of payment of fees (which for a non-EU student is only the regional tax and the EUR 16 stamp). Foreign-citizenship students must enrol IN PERSON at the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80, and cannot use SegrePass. (6) FOR THE STUDY PLAN (after enrolment, by 31 October): students taking one of the three standard tracks need only notify the Student Office of the chosen track. An individual study plan requires the department's Microsoft Forms submission with (a) the "autocertificazione storico" of the bachelor career downloadable from SegrePass, (b) the same for the master's career if not a first submission, and (c) the completed "Modulo A". A study plan including the Minor in Space Economy uses a separate form e-mailed to the Coordinator, copied to Prof. Massimo Viscardi. The programme's own website publishes NO fee page of its own. SHORT ANSWER FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: this degree is close to free. Non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus a EUR 16 stamp; EU non-Italian citizens pay a flat EUR 200 contribution plus the regional tax and stamp. Realistic 2026/27 totals: roughly EUR 167 per year for a non-EU student and roughly EUR 367 per year for an EU non-Italian student. THE BINDING RULES (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27, "Esoneri parziali"): "stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio ... e l'imposta di bollo, entro il termine ordinario di scadenza per il versamento della I rata"; "europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR." For Italian students the ISEEU system applies instead: first-year students are exempt with ISEEU up to EUR 30,000, above which a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those filing no ISEEU declaration. REGIONAL RIGHT-TO-STUDY TAX BANDS 2026/27 (D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026): EUR 130.00 for ISEEU up to 25,500 and for students from particularly poor countries under art. 13 c. 5 DPCM 9 April 2001; EUR 151.00 for ISEEU between 25,500.01 and 51,000 AND for students whose household resides abroad; EUR 173.00 for ISEEU above 51,000 or no ISEEU declaration. Stamp duty EUR 16.00. BUDGET EUR 151 IF YOUR FAMILY LIVES ABROAD — that is the band the Guida assigns explicitly to internationally resident households. INSTALMENTS: 1st (60% + regional tax + stamp) from 16 July and by 2026-11-02; 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01; 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30. Late-enrolment surcharges of EUR 50 (to 15 January 2027) and EUR 110 (from 16 January 2027). uncertainty_notes: 1) THE BIGGEST RISK: DOES A NON-EU APPLICANT NEED B2 ITALIAN? This is unresolved on unina.it and it is decisive. The programme's own Didactic Regulations require only CEFR B1 in ITALIAN **OR** ENGLISH (and waive even that for holders of a degree taught in Italian or English). But the University's non-EU pre-enrolment rules require B2 ITALIAN "if you choose a three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course in ITALIAN", with the English-taught exemption drafted as covering only "three-year, five-year or single-cycle" courses. This degree is officially "bilingue (italiana, inglese)", is tagged ENG/ITA on the orientation portal, and is NOT listed among the English-taught master's degrees in the International Course Catalogue. A non-EU applicant should therefore assume the Italian B2 requirement (or the University-arranged remote interview) MAY be applied, and must confirm in writing with pre-enrolment@unina.it and michele.grassi@unina.it before booking any language test. Because the Italian test result has to be certified inside the Universitaly pre-enrolment application, discovering this late costs a full intake year. 2) THE PROGRAMME IS BILINGUAL, NOT ENGLISH-TAUGHT — AND ONLY ONE OF THE THREE TRACKS IS FULLY DELIVERABLE IN ENGLISH. Aeronautics has ZERO asterisked (English) modules among its four compulsory first-year courses; Fluid Dynamics and Propulsion has one of four; Space has four of four plus an all-English Table B3. Any prospective student who cannot follow Italian is confined, in practice, to the SPACE specialisation. No unina.it page states this conclusion explicitly — it is derived by summing the asterisked modules across the 2026/2027 study-plan tables and the Didactic Regulations annexes. 3) COORDINATOR — DIRECT CONFLICT BETWEEN OFFICIAL UNINA.IT SOURCES. The central unina.it course record lists "Coordinatore: Prof. Gennaro CARDONE", whereas the orientation portal (updated for a.y. 2026/2027), the programme's own Student Guide and the University's International Course Catalogue all name Prof. MICHELE GRASSI. Grassi is almost certainly current; the central record appears not to have been updated. This matters more than usual here, because the Coordinator is the person who evaluates foreign qualifications and signs the pre-acceptance letter. Use michele.grassi@unina.it. 4) CURRENCY: 2026/2027 vs 2025/2026. The orientation-portal course sheet is explicitly "Updated 2026/2027" and its study-plan accordion is labelled "Study Plan. 2026/2027", but the DEPARTMENT's own pages were still headed "Manifesto Laurea Magistrale A.A. 2025/2026" at the time of research, and the newest published Didactic Regulations are those "in vigore a partire dall'a.a. 2025-2026". The two sources agree on structure, tracks and the asterisk rule but not on every detail (see next note). No 2026/2027 Regolamento Didattico or Guida dello Studente had been published. 5) A CREDIT-VALUE DISCREPANCY. The 2026/2027 orientation-portal tables list "Aeroelasticity (9 ECTS*)" in Table B1 (Aeronautics) but "Aeroelasticity (6 ECTS*)" in Table B2 (Fluid Dynamics and Propulsion); the 2025/2026 Didactic Regulations annex gives 6 CFU in both. Treat 6 CFU as the more likely figure and check the current Manifesto. 6) FINAL-EXAM PRESENTATION LENGTH: 15 vs 12 MINUTES. The Didactic Regulations say "La presentazione ha una durata compresa di norma in 15 minuti"; the orientation portal says "The presentation usually lasts 12 minutes". Trivial in itself, but it shows the two sources are maintained independently. 7) THE ADMISSION-FORM LINKS ARE BROKEN. The programme's orientation page routes "(admission of graduates)" to https://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/modulistica-studenti/ (which offers only a further link to the Collegio degli Studi di Ingegneria, from which no admission form could be retrieved) and "(pre-evaluation for lower average)" to a legacy URL that returns HTTP 404. The actual application forms could not be enumerated from unina.it. Request them from uff.didattica.dii@unina.it. 8) NO GRADE-CONVERSION RULE IS PUBLISHED. The personal-preparation gate turns on a CFU-weighted average of at least 24/30, but no unina.it page explains how a foreign grading scale is converted to Italian thirtieths for this purpose — the single most consequential unknown for an international applicant after the language question. 9) NO LIST OF FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS DEEMED EQUIVALENT TO L-9. The requirement is "la laurea nella classe ... L-9 o titolo equipollente", and the escape route for a foreign transcript is the CCD's discretionary power to recognise "equivalenze di crediti di settori scientifico disciplinari differenti ... sulla base dei contenuti di specifici insegnamenti". Nothing is published about how that discretion is exercised, how long it takes, or who sits on the investigating commission. The 18-CFU core-aerospace sub-requirement is the most likely stumbling block for a general mechanical or physics graduate. 10) THE PUBLISHED ADMISSION TEST IS ITALIAN-ONLY. The question bank at Test_Ammissione_Media_Insufficiente_LM_Aerospaziale.pdf — five sections covering flight mechanics, aerodynamics, aerospace propulsion, aerospace systems and aerospace structures — is written entirely in Italian, with no English version published. An applicant below 24/30 who cannot read Italian faces a serious problem, and no unina.it page says whether an English version would be provided on request. 11) THE LANGUAGE APTITUDE TEST HAS NO PUBLISHED FORMAT. Art. 5 imposes a "test di idoneita" on applicants without a qualifying degree or a B1 Italian/English certificate, but no date, venue, format, examiner or pass mark is published anywhere on unina.it. 12) NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DOCUMENT CHECKLIST AND NO INTERNATIONAL ADMISSIONS PAGE. Unlike several other Federico II master's degrees, this programme publishes no annual admission-rules sheet in English, no evaluation timetable and no international-applicant checklist, so required_documents is assembled from University-level sources and the Segreteria could request additional items. 13) NO ENGLISH-CERTIFICATE PROVIDER LIST OR RECENCY RULE. For the 3-CFU "further language knowledge" recognition the sources say only "an English language certificate at level B2 (CEFR), obtained at an accredited centre outside the University". No list of accepted awarding bodies and no two-year recency limit (such as Mathematical Engineering imposes) is published for this degree. 14) NO SEAT FIGURE IS PUBLISHED and none is expected, since the course is not numero programmato; the non-EU contingent for open-access degrees is declared on universitaly.it, which lies outside this task's unina.it-only source restriction.
